# Reading in the Washington Post homicide data

```{r read_data}
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
# Read in the homicide data from the Washington Post github repository ---------
# (saved as a .csv) and combine city and state into a new column ---------------
homicides <- read_csv("../data/homicide-data.csv") %>% 
  mutate(city_name = paste0(city, ", ", state))
```
# Filtering to only include Baltimore, MD

```{r filter_baltimore}
library(lubridate)
# Filter to only include Baltimore, MD, convert reported_date to a date class, -
# and add year and month -------------------------------------------------------
baltimore_homicides <- homicides %>% 
  filter(city_name == "Baltimore, MD") %>% 
  mutate(reported_date = ymd(reported_date)) %>% 
  mutate(month = month(reported_date),
         year = year(reported_date))
```

# Counting monthly homicides in Baltimore, MD

```{r count_homicides}
# Create a new dataframe that counts the monthly homicides ---------------------
monthly_homicides <- baltimore_homicides %>% 
  mutate(date = make_date(year = year, month = month)) %>% 
  group_by(date) %>% 
  count() %>% 
  ungroup()
# Add monthly homicide count and season data to a new results dataframe --------
results <- monthly_homicides %>% 
  mutate(month = month(date)) %>% 
  mutate(season = case_when(month %in% c(5:10) ~ "Summer",
                            month %in% c(1:4, 11:12) ~ "Winter"))
```

# Plotting monthly homicides in Baltimore, MD

```{r plot_homicides, fig.width=900/96, fig.height=267/96}
library(ggplot2)
library(ggthemes)
ggplot(data = results,
       mapping = aes(x = date,
                     y = n,
                     fill = season)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("lightgray", "lightblue")) +
  labs(x = "Date",
       y = "Monthly homicides",
       title = "Homicides in Baltimore, MD") +
  theme_dark()
```
